Alex — following up with the more technical details Ben promised. I pulled together the short checklist below and a link to a doc with code samples: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-integration-guide

1) SDK setup & auth - SDKs (Python / Node / Java) provide helpers for auth. Supported auth modes: API keys (simple), OAuth2 client credentials (recommended for service-account flows), and mTLS (for Private deployments).
- For service accounts: exchange your internal service principal for a Redwood short-lived token via OAuth client_credentials; rotate tokens regularly.
- Per-API-key quotas apply; recommend separate keys per environment (dev/stage/prod).

2) Routing & region failover - Use the SDK routing policy to prefer a region (us-west) and configure fallback to another region (us-east) with automatic model-variant fallback.

3) Structured output and tool calling - We support function/tool calling and structured outputs (JSON schema enforcement). For actions with side effects (e.g., create-ticket), treat the call as idempotent by passing a client_request_id header that you can dedupe on your side if an endpoint is retried.

4) Embeddings + reranker guidance - Batch embedding requests (recommended batch size 32–128 items depending on payload size); prefer async batch endpoints for bulk indexing. For reranking: retrieve top-k candidates via sparse or semantic search, then call the reranker model with the top candidates and a single request to get final scores. Reranker traffic is low QPS but higher token per call.

5) Rate limiting, retries & idempotency (concrete) - Headers we return: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and Retry-After when applicable.
- On 429: honor Retry-After if present. If not present, use exponential backoff with full jitter: base = 250ms, multiply by 2^attempts up to cap = 5s, add random jitter up to base.
- Idempotency: include X-Client-Request-Id or Idempotency-Key for any write/side-effect call. The server will return a 409 if an idempotent operation conflicts.
- Retries: safe retries for idempotent calls only. For non-idempotent calls, use client-side dedupe + idempotency keys and keep retries to a minimum.

6) Streaming & partial failures - For token streaming, retries should be handled at the request level (reconnect and resume where possible). If a stream aborted after tokens were generated, use client_request_id to indicate whether partial tokens were accepted downstream; otherwise replay may create duplicates.

I'll bring code snippets to the deep-dive, including Python examples for setting X-Client-Request-Id and parsing rate-limit headers.

—Marissa

Alex — good questions. Quick answers and final proposed commitments before the deep-dive Tuesday 10am PT:

- Rate-limit buckets: we expose separate effective buckets for generation, embeddings, and async batch endpoints. Headers reflect the bucket for the endpoint you called (X-RateLimit-Limit / Remaining / Reset). For hosted customers it's per-API-key by default; for enterprise/dedicated we can provide org-level buckets and custom quotas. We also surface soft-limits (warnings) vs hard quotas (429).

- Idempotency header: X-Client-Request-Id (or Idempotency-Key) is optional but strongly recommended for any call that triggers a downstream effect. If retries arrive with different ids you should treat them as distinct requests; the server will not dedupe across differing ids. To guarantee single-effect semantics, always reuse the same id for retransmissions of the same logical operation.

- Streaming resume: we recommend emitting a client_request_id and persisting last-processed-token positions on your side. If a stream aborts, open a new request with the same id and a resume-offset; the server will attempt to continue if the underlying model cache still holds the context. If not resumable, the server will return an informative code and you can replay non-side-effect-only portions safely. We'll demo resume patterns in the SE deep-dive.

1) I'll provision a sandbox API key scoped to a dev project (limited quota) — you should receive credentials by EOD tomorrow.
